instructions.name: add_juror
docs: Seats a juror: encrypted (id, key). The ciphertext can come from the juror's
own browser key, so the authority relays a seat whose ballot key it never sees.
Authority only (stands in for sortition + identity attestation).

instructions.name: bet
docs: Stakes `lamports` on YES (`yes = true`) or NO while the court is unresolved.
Bets are public; the court authority mirrors bettors into the court with
`record_positions`, so a bettor who also sits on the jury is excluded.

instructions.name: cast
docs: Casts or overwrites an encrypted ballot (id, key, new_key, yes). It only counts
inside MPC if `key` is the seat's current key; a non-zero `new_key` rotates it.
Any payer can relay it, so the signer reveals nothing about who the juror is.

instructions.name: claim
docs: Pays a bettor after the verdict: winners split the whole pool pro rata;
a tie, an empty winning side or an incomplete verdict refunds every stake.

instructions.name: create_court
docs: Opens a dispute court for one market and queues `init_court` (empty state).

instructions.name: create_market
docs: Opens a YES/NO pari-mutuel market that settles on `court`'s verdict.

instructions.name: record_positions
docs: Records up to 6 encrypted identities as holding a position in this market
(unused entries encrypt 0). Authority only: it mirrors positions read from
the market's chain state (Panta `UserPosition` accounts in the demo).

instructions.name: reset_pending
docs: Releases the lock after an aborted computation (its callback never cleared it).
Authority only.

instructions.name: resolve
docs: Tallies conflict-free ballots. Authority only.

errors.name: ComputationPending
errors.msg: Another computation is still pending for this court

errors.name: MarketTooLong
errors.msg: Market text is longer than 64 bytes

errors.name: SideMismatch
errors.msg: A bettor can only add to the side they already backed

errors.name: WrongCourt
errors.msg: Market belongs to a different court

types.name: AddJurorV3Output
docs: The output of the callback instruction. Provided as a struct with ordered fields
as anchor does not support tuples and tuple structs yet.

types.name: CastV3Output
docs: The output of the callback instruction. Provided as a struct with ordered fields
as anchor does not support tuples and tuple structs yet.

types.name: ClockAccount
docs: An account storing the current network epoch

types.name: ComputationDefinitionAccount
docs: An account representing a [ComputationDefinition] in a MXE.

types.name: ComputationDefinitionMeta
docs: A computation definition for execution in a MXE.

types.name: ComputationSignature
docs: The signature of a computation defined in a [ComputationDefinition].

fields.name: state
docs: Encrypted court state; must stay right after `bump` (offset 9).

fields.name: pending
docs: A computation is queued and its callback has not landed yet.

fields.name: incomplete
docs: A slot overflowed, so the conflict check may be incomplete; markets refund.

types.name: Epoch
docs: The network epoch

types.name: InitCourtV3Output
docs: The output of the callback instruction. Provided as a struct with ordered fields
as anchor does not support tuples and tuple structs yet.

types.name: LeaderChoice
docs: The computation chosen by a node to be executed when the node is leader.

types.name: LeaderInfo
docs: The information about a node.

types.name: LeaderSelector
docs: To select a Leader.
Uses the greatest divisors method: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%27Hondt_method

types.name: MXEAccount
docs: A MPC Execution Environment.

types.name: MxeStatus
docs: The status of an MXE.

types.name: NodeMetadata
docs: location as [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://www.iso.org/iso-3166-country-codes.html) country code

types.name: NodeRef
docs: A reference to a node in the cluster.
The offset is to derive the Node Account.

types.name: Output
docs: An output of a computation.
We currently don't support encrypted outputs yet since encrypted values are passed via
data objects.

types.name: Parameter
docs: A parameter of a computation.
We differentiate between plaintext and encrypted parameters and data objects.
Plaintext parameters are directly provided as their value.
Encrypted parameters are provided as an offchain reference to the data.
Data objects are provided as a reference to the data object account.

types.name: SetUnset
docs: Utility struct to store a value that needs to be set by a certain number of participants (keys
in our case). Once all participants have set the value, the value is considered set and we only
store it once.
